items.title: SK하이닉스, 자사주 매수 주문량 35만주→70만주 확대
items.snippet: SK하이닉스[000660]가 최근 주가 하락에 대응해 자기주식 매입 속도를 높인다.28일 한국거래소의 자기주식매매 신청내역에 따르면 SK하이닉스는 오는 30일 장중 자기주식 70만주를 매수하겠다고 신고했다.이는 직전 거래일인 27일까지 하루 35만주였던 매수 주문량을 두 배로 늘린 것이다.최근 주가 하락으로 기업가치 대비 저평가가 심화했다는 판단에 따라 기존 자사주 취득 계획의 집행 속도를 높이려는 조치다.SK하이닉스 주가는 지난 6월 25일 장중 298만7천원까지 올랐으나 이후 하락세를 보이며 전날 111만원에 거래를 마쳤다.S

items.title: 롯데쇼핑 해외사업 희비…베트남은 효자, 인니는 아픈 손가락

items.title: 박홍근 “법사위가 상원이냐”… 민주당 장관이 與의원 이례적 비판

items.title: ‘하명 징계’ 싸움에 리더십 실종 국힘… 장동혁 “한동훈 복당해도 다시 징계”

items.snippet: 1994년 우크라이나 서부 도시 테르노필의 한 치과. 열다섯 살쯤 된 남학생이 뒤로 젖혀지지도 않는 의자에 앉아 신경 치료를 받고 있었다. 통증을 줄이기 위해 마취를 해야 했지만, 나라 전체가 겪는 경제난 탓에 병원에는 마취제가 없었다. 그런데도 학생은 의자 손잡이를 꼭 잡은 채 얼굴을 조금 찌푸릴 뿐 소리 한 번 지르지 않고 묵묵히 견뎌냈다. 단기 의료 봉사로 우크라이나를 방문해 이를 지켜보던 당시 34세 치과 의사 강지헌씨는 다짐했다. 의료 인프라가 열악한 이 나라에 다시 와서 환자들의 아픔을 조금이라도 덜어주겠다고. 2년 후 강씨는 테르노필에 갔다. 이번에는 단기 봉사가 아니었다. 선의로 내디딘 발걸음이었지만, 뭐 하나 순탄치 않았다. 외국인 의사에게 의료 면허를 잘 내주지 않는 관행 탓에 여러 가지 제약이 뒤따랐다. 이렇게 시작된 그의...

items.title: 하나의 칼집에 박힌 두 자루의 칼
items.snippet: 지난주 내내 특별전 준비로 전시실 작업이 있었다. 전시실 내 인테리어 공사가 마무리되어 유물을 전시실로 옮겨 와서 배치하는 일이다. 전시품 배치는 미리 구상하고 평면도와 입면도를 보며 여러 번 검토하지만, 실제로 유물을 놓아 보면 이미지로 시뮬레이션해 본 것과는 달라 받침대나 위치를 바꾸기도 하고, 일부 유물은 추가로 받치고 고정하기도 한다. 지난주에는 대학수학능력시험과 관련하여 나날이 강력해지는 AI의 위력을 실감할 수 있었기에, 전시실에서 지난한 작업을 하던 일부 직원들은 약간의 소외감을 느끼기도 한 것 같다. 그러나 디지털이 만들어낸 가상의 세계가 커질수록 물질성을 직접 느끼는 박물관 경험은 더욱 귀하게 쓰일 것이라 믿고 있다.

items.title: 검찰 이빨 다 뽑은 이재명 시대… 절대 ‘피해자’가 되지 맙시다
items.snippet: 작년 10월 20일, 김창민 영화감독은 아들과 함께 경기 구리시의 식당을 찾았다가 다른 테이블에 있던 이들과 소음 문제로 다툰 끝에 뇌사 상태에 빠졌다. 사인은 심한 구타로 인한 두개골 골절과 뇌출혈이었는데, 발달장애가 있던 아들은 그 사건을 목격한 뒤 증상이 악화됐단다. 문제는 그 이후 불거졌다. 20·30대 남성 6명이 김 감독을 위협하는 데 가담했고, 그중에는 폭력 전과가 있는 이도 있었지만, 경찰은 단 1명(이씨)만, 그것도 중상해 혐의를 적용해 불구속 송치했다.

items.title: 3주간 스마트폰 없이 지냈더니 기적이 일어났다?
items.snippet: “수능 최하위권이었다. 전국 도보 일주를 하다 스마트폰을 잃어버려 3주간 디지털 디톡스(digital detox·온라인 과의존 해독)를 하게 됐다. 신기한 일이 일어났다. 갑자기 집중력이 높아지고 어려운 글이 이해됐다. 고려대 정외과, 그리고 서울대 치대에 합격했다. 이어 법학적성시험(LEET)에서 사상 첫 만점자로….”

items.title: 수능시험 날의 생각들
items.snippet: 중국과 조선의 과거제도, 일본의 고등문관시험, 우리나라의 고등고시와 행정고시·사법시험 등은 공정한 시험에 의해 신분 상승의 길을 열어 사회적 갈등을 완화하고 정치적 안정을 유지하는 역할을 했습니다. 비록 한계는 있었지만, 가난하거나 권세 없는 집안의 자녀도 자신의 노력과 능력으로 시험을 통해 높은 지위에 오를 수 있다는 희망을 품었기 때문입니다. 이른바 ‘개천에서 용이 난다’는 말도 이러한 믿음의 표현입니다. 어떤 학자는 이런 제도가 없었으면 반란은 더 빈번히 발생했을 것이고, 공산화도 더 쉽게 진행되었을 것이라고도 합니다. 우연일지도 모르지만 실제로 중국의 경우, 과거제도가 폐지된 뒤에 신해혁명이 일어났고 결국 공산화의 길로 들어섰습니다.

items.title: “노력은 부질없고 앞날은 막막”… 번지는 ‘AI 블루’
items.snippet: “요즘 인공지능(AI) 때문에 우울해요. 열심히 노력하는 게 무슨 의미가 있나 싶어서요.”

items.title: 빨래의 완성은 향기?
items.snippet: 갓 빤 수건에서는 기분 좋은 향이 난다. 햇볕에 말린 듯한 포근함에 은은한 꽃향기까지. 그런데 생각해 보면 이상하다. 깨끗한 빨래에는 왜 반드시 좋은 냄새가 나야 할까? 세탁의 목적은 때와 오염을 제거하는 것이지 향기를 입히는 것이 아닌데 말이다.

items.title: 기상 알람은 필요하지만 스마트폰은 안 쓰고 싶다
items.snippet: 지난 5월 일본 가전 회사 발뮤다는 신제품으로 탁상시계 ‘더 클락’을 내놓았다. 스마트폰이 시계 기능은 물론 기상 알람, 타이머 역할까지 대신해 주는 시대에 굳이 수십만 원짜리 시계를 선보인 것이다. 이 시계엔 최신 가전제품들이 앞다퉈 탑재하는 사물인터넷(IoT) 연동이나 음성 인공지능(AI) 기능도 들어 있지 않다. 대신 눈뜨자마자 스마트폰을 집어 들고, 잠들 때도 이를 머리맡에 두는 현대인들이 잠시나마 스마트폰과 거리를 두게 하는 데 초점을 맞췄다. 기존 탁상시계의 알람과 타이머 기능은 그대로 갖추되, 시침과 분침 대신 LED로 시간을 표시해 어두운 공간에서도 시간을 확인할 수 있도록 했다. 또 이른바 ‘백색소음’을 들으며 잠을 청하는 사람들을 위해 빗소리와 귀뚜라미 소리 등 음향 기능을 더했다. 제품 출시 당시 방한한 테라오 겐(53)...

items.title: 이 추위에 야외에서 茶 마시는 사람들
items.snippet: 직장인 한모(33)씨는 주말이면 뜨거운 물이 든 보온병과 휴대용 1인 다기(茶器)를 들고 집 근처 공원으로 간다. 벤치에 작은 천을 깔고 찻잎을 우린 뒤, 1시간가량 여유롭게 차를 마신다. 한씨는 “기온이 떨어져 목도리까지 두르고 집을 나서지만 찬바람 맞으며 따뜻한 차를 마시면 머리가 맑아지고 기분도 한결 상쾌해진다”며 “차가운 공기 속에서 피어오르는 수증기와 찻잎의 향, 따뜻한 잔이 손에 전하는 온기 등 실내에서 경험하기 어려운 정취를 만끽할 수 있다”고 했다. 야외에서 다도를 즐기는 이들이 늘고 있다. ‘야차(野茶)’, ‘야다(야외 다도)’, ‘티크닉(차+피크닉)’이라고도 부른다. 한강공원 잔디밭이나 산, 바닷가 등에 자리를 잡고 직접 우려낸 차를 마시며 풍경을 감상하는 식이다.

items.title: 주식의 신은 이렇게 말했다
items.snippet: 김남우는 주식 고수로 정평이 나 있었지만, 큰 인기는 없었다. 재미없는 말만 입에 달고 살았으니까. “주식은 건실하게 지수 추종만 하면 돼. 미국이 망하지 않는 한 절대로 손해는 안 본다니까.”

items.title: 남들이 다 사 갈까 봐 급히 또 주문했다
items.snippet: 새벽 의림지에 하얀 안개가 꼈다. 둑과 길 위로 걷고 뛰는 이들이 보였다. 바람은 불지 않고 물결도 일지 않았다. 어릴 적 살던 부산 영도에서 밖을 바라보면 늘 일렁이는 파도였다. 오고 가는 커다란 배와 세찬 바람을 맞으면 어린 마음에도 어디론가 떠나고 싶었다. 중년이 되어 의림지 앞에 서니 가슴이 뛰기보다 잔잔해졌다. 그러나 제천에는 이제 KTX가 다닌다. 여전히 조용한 동네이고 사람들은 의뭉스러운 충청도 사투리를 쓰지만, 의림지에서 제천역으로 향하는 국도 사이로 시끌벅적한 가게들도 여럿 생겼다. 저수지 주변을 한참 걷고 온 탓인지 가볍게 빵 몇 조각만 있어도 충분할 것 같았다. 아침 8시, 문을 연 빵집을 찾다 ‘솔솔’이라는 곳을 찾았다. 발효빵을 비롯해 식사빵을 주로 파는 듯 보였다. 선택지가 없었다. 대로변 아담한 빵집에는 작은 주차장...

items.title: 트레비 분수의 동전이 줄어든 이유
items.snippet: 이탈리아 로마 트레비 분수에 동전 던져본 적 있으십니까. 이 분수에 동전을 던지면 로마에 다시 올 수 있거나 소원이 이루어진다는 속설이 있죠. 1732년부터 30년에 걸쳐 만든 트레비 분수는 로마 여행의 필수 코스로 꼽힙니다.

items.title: 여우 본성 바꾼 실험… 과학은 이념보다 강했다
items.snippet: 1958년 구(舊)소련의 저명한 유전학자인 드미트리 벨랴예프(1917~1985)가 모스크바 국립대를 우등 졸업해 전도가 유망했던 젊은 동물생리학자 류드밀라 트루트(1933~2024)를 만났다. 벨랴예프는 그녀에게 대뜸 “여우를 개로 만들고 싶다”고 말했다. 온순한 여우끼리 교배시켜 늑대가 사람을 따르는 개가 된 과정을 재현하자는 황당한 제안이었다.

items.title: 월급은 짧고 밤은 길다… 졸린 눈 부릅뜨는 ‘야간 경제’
items.snippet: 야경 너머에 누군가의 야근이 있다. 밤잠 물리치려는 몸부림, 편의점만 가 봐도 알 수 있다. 지난 1년간 심야 시간대(오후 10시~오전 4시) 국내 편의점에서 드러난 괄목할 변화는 ‘에너지 음료’와 ‘밥’ 판매 추이. 시장조사 기업 엠브레인 딥데이터에 따르면, 지난 6월 기준 에너지 음료 구매 건수는 약 733만건으로 지난해 같은 기간보다 41.5%, 밥류는 약 291만건으로 38.7% 급증했다. 야밤에 뇌를 깨우고 식량을 입에 밀어 넣는다. 힘써야 하므로.

items.title: AI가 하는 다이어트 조언 효과적일까
items.snippet: 점심으로 먹은 비빔밥 사진을 AI에 보여주면 몇 초 만에 열량을 알려준다. 달걀프라이 아래 깔린 고사리도 알아보고, 고추장을 조금 덜 넣으라는 조언까지 곁들인다. 내 몸에 맞는 음식을 골라 주기까지 한다. 팔에 연속혈당측정기(CGM)를 붙이고 대변으로 장내 미생물까지 분석해 정밀 맞춤 영양을 제공하는 기업이 국내외에서 주목받고 있다. AI로 무슨 일이든 할 수 있을 것 같은 세상이다. 사진, 혈당, 장내 미생물로 분석해 내놓는 AI의 조언은 얼마나 효과적일까?

items.title: 산타도 놀라겠네, 크리스마스 케이크가 60만원
items.snippet: 크리스마스 케이크가 또다시 역대 최고가를 경신했다. 서울신라호텔이 크리스마스 시즌을 맞아 60만원짜리 ‘더 파이니스트 리저브’를 선보였다. 이 호텔에서 지난해 최고가였던 ‘더 파이니스트 럭셔리’(50만원)보다 10만원이 올랐다. 파티시에 3명이 화이트·블랙 트러플과 프랑스 디저트 와인 샤토 디켐 등 최고급 식재료를 사용해 하루 최대 3개 만든다.

items.title: 매수 사이드카에도 코스닥, 8%대 가파른 급등세…700선 회복

items.title: 건물 한 층에 3700명분… 서울 한복판 친구집은 ‘대마 공장’이었다
items.snippet: 친구 사이인 A(29)씨와 B(29)씨는 지난해 1월부터 서울 성북구 주택가 건물 4층을 통째로 빌려 대마를 재배해 오다 적발돼 최근 중대범죄수사청에 구속됐다. 중수청은 현장에서 건조 대마 1.1㎏과 재배 중인 대마 33주를 압수했다. 3700명이 동시에 투약할 수 있는 분량이었다. C(33)씨는 지난해 3월부터 올 5월까지 서울 중랑구 자택에서 대마를 재배하다가 적발돼 징역 1년에 집행유예 2년을 선고받았다. 적발 당시 C씨가 보유한 대마는 587g으로, 1200명이 투약할 수 있는 분량이었다. C씨는 자기 집 1층 세탁실 뒤편과 2층 다락방에서 대마를 재배했다.

items.title: 해외 명품가구가 반값? 600명이 물건 못 받아
items.snippet: 유명 온라인 가구 판매 쇼핑몰 ‘바우트’는 해외 명품 가구를 정가보다 50~60% 저렴하게 판매하면서 소비자 사이에서 입소문을 탔다. 그러나 1년여 전부터 소비자가 결제한 가구 배송을 미루기 시작하더니 최근에는 사무실을 폐쇄하고 연락이 두절됐다. 결국 피해자들이 바우트 대표 박모(46)씨를 사기 혐의로 경찰에 고소했다. 바우트에 가구를 주문하고 결제까지 했다가 물건을 받지 못한 피해자는 600명이 넘는 것으로 알려졌다.

items.title: 인천 남동산업단지 공장서 화재… 직원 1명 숨져
items.snippet: 26일 오후 12시 15분쯤 인천 남동구 고잔동 남동국가산업단지 내 자동차 부품 공장에서 불이 나 검은 연기가 치솟고 있다. 이날 화재로 직원 1명이 숨지고, 3층 규모 공장 건물이 다 탔다. 소방당국은 화재 발생 3시간 49분 만에 불을 완전히 껐다.

items.title: 尹 ‘한덕수 재판 위증’, 대법서 무죄 확정
items.snippet: 대법원 1부(주심 마용주 대법관)는 26일 한덕수 전 국무총리 내란 사건 재판에서 위증한 혐의로 기소된 윤석열 전 대통령에게 무죄를 선고했다. 윤 전 대통령이 지난 7월 ‘고위공직자범죄수사처 체포 방해’ 사건으로 징역 7년을 확정받은 뒤 나온 두 번째 대법원 판결이다.

items.title: “나눔 함께해요” 자선냄비 전달식
items.snippet: 한국구세군과 휘슬러코리아가 26일 오전 서울 중구 서울광장에서 ‘2026 사랑ON 자선냄비 전달식’을 열었다. 아이들이 자선냄비 앞에서 구세군 종을 울리고 있다.

items.title: 여학생 절반 “스트레스” 남학생의 1.5배 달해
items.snippet: 술을 마시는 중·고교 여학생의 절반 이상은 한 번에 평균 소주 3잔 이상을 마시는 ‘위험 음주’를 하는 것으로 나타났다. 전체 청소년의 음주율은 낮아졌지만, 술을 마시는 여학생의 위험 음주율은 2023년부터 4년 연속 증가했다.

items.title: 악성 민원 ‘진상 학부모’ 학교에 발 못 붙이게 한다
items.snippet: 정부가 교권을 보호하고 무고성 아동 학대 신고를 줄이기 위해 관련 법 개정에 나선다. 교권을 침해한 학부모는 상당 기간 학교 출입을 못 하게 하는 제도도 도입한다.

items.title: ‘서울 최대 재개발’ 한남3구역 23년 만에 첫삽
items.snippet: 서울 최대 재개발 사업지인 용산구 한남3구역이 26일 공사를 시작했다. 2003년 뉴타운으로 지정된 지 23년 만이다. 한남뉴타운 5개 구역 중 첫 착공이다. 2030년 한강변 낡은 주택가가 5970가구 아파트 단지로 바뀔 전망이다.

items.title: “현대차 시설 4년내 가동… 군산을 제2 울산으로”
items.snippet: 김재준(55) 전북 군산시장은 26일 본지 인터뷰에서 “임기 내 현대차그룹 공장이 실제로 가동되도록 하는 게 목표”라며 “군산을 제2의 울산으로 만들겠다”고 했다.

items.title: “네 개의 심장 소리 듣고 하나도 포기 할 수 없었죠”
items.snippet: 지난 18일 오전 11시 경기도 안양의 한 주거용 오피스텔 거실에 생후 15개월 된 네 쌍둥이 태이·채이·래이·재이가 함께 놀고 있었다. ‘태채래재 네 쌍둥이’로 불리는 이들 중 둘째 채이가 딸, 나머지 셋은 아들이다. 아이들은 거실을 기어다니다 서로 다리를 잡아보기도 하고, 한참 눈을 맞추기도 했다. 한 아이가 웃으면 다 같이 “까르르” 웃고, 한 아이가 손뼉 치면 다른 아이들도 따라 쳤다. 엄마 조세린(35)씨가 “이제 낮잠 잘 시간이야” 하자, 아빠 국은혁(36)씨가 아이들을 차례로 침대로 옮겼다. 처음엔 떼쓰던 아이들이 5분쯤 지나니 다 같이 잠이 들었다. 조씨는 “아이가 넷이라 자기들끼리 놀고, 잠도 침대에서 다 함께 잔다”고 했다.

items.title: [우리 아기가 태어났어요] 장하영·박종혁 아들 수호 외
items.snippet: 온 가족에게 기쁨을 안겨 준 아기의 탄생을 알려주세요. 홈페이지 주소 입력창에 아가야안녕.com이라고 입력하면 됩니다. 매일유업 육아 정보 사이트 매일아이(maeili.com)를 통해서도 접속할 수 있습니다. 추첨을 통해 출산 소식과 사진이 지면에 실린 가족에게는 ①케이크 구매권 ②엄마와 아이를 위한 매일두 포인트 3만원 ③출산 소식을 생일 날짜 본지 1면에 담은 PDF 파일 ④조선일보 1개월 무료 구독권을 드립니다. 당첨자 중 한 가족을 선정하여 해당 지면을 고급 프레임에 담아 제공하는 조선일보 리프린트도 제작해 드립니다. 홈페이지에서는 균형 영양식 메디웰 2만원 할인 혜택도 드리고 있습니다.

items.title: [알립니다] 우리 아이 출생 소식 액자에 담아 간직하세요
items.snippet: 조선일보에 실린 아기 출생 소식, 본인이나 지인의 인터뷰·사진 기사를 영원히 추억으로 간직하세요. 조선일보는 독자가 원하는 신문 지면을 그대로 고급 액자에 담아 드리는 ‘조선일보 리프린트’ 서비스를 합니다. 매주 ‘아이가 행복입니다’ 지면에 소개된 한 가족을 추첨해 리프린트를 선물로 드립니다. 지난 20일 ‘우리 아기가 태어났어요’ 코너에 실린 김연서 양이 이번 주 주인공입니다. 자세한 내용은 홈페이지(reprint.chosun.com)에서 확인할 수 있습니다.

items.snippet: 성균관대 출신 언론인 모임 성균언론인회(회장 이종환)는 26일 ‘2026 자랑스러운 성균언론인상’ 언론 부문에 김용준 한국경제 편집국장과 권남근 헤럴드경제 편집국장을 선정했다. 대외 부문에는 오광수 법무법인 대륙아주 대표변호사와 윤영선 전 관세청장이 선정됐다. 시상식은 30일 오후 7시 성균관대 600주년 기념관 조병두홀에서 열릴 예정이다.

items.snippet: 아시아기자협회(AJA·이사장 이기우)는 25일 서울 한국프레스센터 20층 무궁화실에서 창립 22주년 정기 이사회를 열고 홍진욱 전 주싱가포르 대한민국 대사와 김건일 전 한라일보 대표이사를 신임 이사로 선임했다.

items.title: 한국여성단체협의회, 제61회 전국여성대회 개최
items.snippet: 올해로 61회를 맞은 전국여성대회가 26일 서울 코엑스에서 열렸다. 대한민국 여성의 사회 참여와 권익을 높이기 위해 1962년 시작한 이 대회는 한국여성단체협의회(여협) 주최로 열리는데, 전국의 여성 지도자들이 한자리에 모여 사회적 현안을 논의하는 행사다.

items.title: 토종 반도체 포토레지스트 원소재 업계도 '호황'
items.snippet: 반도체 포토레지스트(PR)의 원재료를 공급하는 주요 업체 실적이 크게 개선된 것으로 나타났다. PR 사용량이 늘었고 국내에 공장을 둔 해외 PR 제조사도 국산 원재료를 일부 채택하면서 공급량이 늘어났기 때문이다.26일 디일렉 취재를 종합하면 켐트로스, 미원상사, 경인양행, 삼양엔씨켐, 이엔에프테크놀로지 등 국내 PR 원소재 공급사 5곳의 올해 3분기 매출과 영업이익이 모두 전년 동기 대비 개선됐다.성장 폭이 가장 큰 곳은 켐트로스다. 3분기 매출이 253억원으로 93.6% 늘었다. 영업손익은 6억원 적자에서 40억원 흑자로 돌아섰다

items.title: Brightening spin- and parity-forbidden interlayer excitons through rhombohedral stacking
items.abstract: Brightened symmetry-forbidden excitons can provide critical information about the electronic structure and many-body interactions in semiconductors. Recently, interlayer atomic registry has emerged as a new way to control atomically thin layered materials in both ground and excited states. Here we show that the rhombohedral stacking in a 3R-MoS_2 homobilayer can brighten two symmetry-forbidden interlayer excitons: one is a spin-unlike 1s exciton and the other is a parity-odd 2p exciton. The nature of these interlayer excitons is revealed by their gfactors as well as the hybridization patterns observed when they are tuned to resonate with intralayer excitons. Surprisingly, the hybridized 2p exciton exhibits a constructive quantum interference between the acquired transition dipoles, revealing a hidden gauge-invariant phase contrast between the constituent electronic states. items.abstract: Charge noise from two-level fluctuators (TLFs) limits gate fidelities in semiconductor spin qubits, yet locating individual fluctuators within a device remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a spatial triangulation method that combines the gate dependence of a TLF's detuning with the chemical potential shifts it induces in a sensing dot. Applying this method to previously reported measurements from a gated Si/SiGe quantum dot device, we use electrostatic simulations to jointly constrain the fluctuator's three-dimensional position and the magnitude of its electric dipole moment. items.title: Direct generation of N00N states with layered semiconductors
items.abstract: Photonic N00N states enable phase sensing beyond the classical limit, but their generation conventionally relies on interferometric manipulation of photons using bulk optical components. Here we demonstrate the direct generation of a family of tunable two-photon polarization N00N states from a subwavelength-thick 3R-MoS2 flake. For propagation along the optic axis, the in-plane crystal symmetry allows all symmetry permitted spontaneous parametric down-conversion pathway to interfere coherently, while the large second-order nonlinearity provides sufficient brightness at submicrometer thickness without phase matching. The pump polarization sets the basis of the N00N state or equivalently a two-photon Holland-Burnett state without altering its structure or the generation efficiency. items.title: AFM metrology for 3D high aspect ratio semiconductor structures
items.abstract: Transistors have long been the foundation of the semiconductor industry, with continuous architectural innovations enabling the scaling of integrated circuits while maintaining high performance. Advancements in deposition and lithographic techniques have further expanded design possibilities, while increasing structural complexity demands stricter process control. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) offers a rapid and reliable metrology solution, providing high-resolution measurements and robust statistical analysis of critical parameters. In this work, we present clearly resolved individual profiles of lines and spaces in high aspect ratio (HAR) gate all around FET (GAAFET)-type structures on both the nanosheet (NS) region and in the isolation region between the nanosheets and we present a comprehensive statistical evaluation of their critical dimensions.

items.title: High-Precision Photometry with a scientific CMOS Camera: III Lab and on-Sky testing of Andor Toran-26B
items.abstract: Scientific CMOS cameras are increasingly used in modern astronomy, offering CCD-like performance with lower power use, faster readout, and reduced cost. We evaluate the photometric precision of the Toran-26B camera, featuring the IMX571 sensor from Sony, a new CMOS camera from Andor Technology, through laboratory and on-sky tests in its two modes: high well capacity (HWC) and low noise (LN). Key metrics include read noise, dark current, photo and dark signal non-uniformity, quantum efficiency, and window transmittance. The median read noise is 1.07\,e$^-$ (LN) and 2.79\,e$^-$ (HWC). Bias shows minor dark signal non-uniformity: 0.076\,e$^-$ (LN), 0.173\,e$^-$ (HWC). Pixel well depth reaches 15700\,e$^-$ (LN) and 50000\,e$^-$ (HWC), with dynamic ranges of 83.39\,dB and 85.05\,dB, respectively. items.title: Real-Time Cryo-CMOS Photon-Number Readout from a Single SNSPD
items.abstract: Measurements leveraging the intrinsic photon-number resolution of Superconducting Nanostrip Single-Photon Detectors (SNSPDs) have recently gained traction due to the simplicity of the detector design. Intrinsic photon-number measurement schemes using SNSPDs encode the photon-number information in picosecond signal timing; these systems thus require high bandwidth readout and sensitive electrical measurement equipment. We show a cryogenic electronic circuit operating close to the SNSPD in the cryostat, which can isolate single-photon detection events directly from the SNSPD signal. This reduces the latency of the photon-number readout to (13.9 $\pm$ 0.3) ns, which enables feedforward operations based on intrinsic photon-number measurements with low latency.

items.title: Bayesian Calibration of Effective Material Parameters in Electric Machine Stators
items.abstract: Efficiency-driven faster switching by wide-bandgap semiconductor devices increases electromagnetic interference (EMI) in electric vehicles (EVs). Mitigating this EMI becomes more complex as system components grow. Therefore, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is assessed early via system-level simulation of the EV powertrain. A key EMC-critical quantity is the impedance of the electric drive machine, forming a major part of the EMI propagation path. Finite element (FE) simulations are typically used but are computationally expensive and limited by insufficient material property knowledge. We present a surrogate model based Bayesian calibration framework for 3D full-wave FE simulation of an externally excited synchronous motor (EESM) stator. items.abstract: High contact resistance, predominantly stemming from Fermi-level pinning (FLP), becomes a critical bottleneck in the contact engineering of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) based two-dimensional field-effect transistors (2DFETs). Our study re-examines the inherent nature of FLP in 2D semiconductors, particularly focusing on regimes where the material thickness is commensurate with the interface thickness. Through the synergistic application of first-principles calculations and experimental validation via ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), we rigorously establish the metal effective work function (eWF) as the definitive figure of merit for substantiating the Schottky-Mott relation. items.title: Carrier relaxation confines the Bogdanov--Takens degeneracy of an optically injected semiconductor laser
items.abstract: Optically injected semiconductor lasers are forced nonlinear oscillators whose locking boundaries are organized by codimension-two points. We ask which property of the carrier balance permits or forbids a Bogdanov--Takens (BT) point in the standard three-dimensional rate equations. Taking the carrier inversion $n$ as distinguished observable, the rate that enters the spectral conditions is the slope of the gain--loss balance, $ξ=\partial\dot n/\partial n=-2Γ/κ$, where $Γ$ is the damping of the relaxation oscillation and $κ=1+2Bn$ the normalized stimulated-emission factor. The two BT conditions become affine in $ξ$ and imply the exact sum rule $K^{2}=I[1-(1+κ)I]$ between injection amplitude $K$ and intracavity intensity $I$. items.title: From Entropy Source to Stochastic Bit-Stream: Low-Cost Converters for True-Random Stochastic Computing
items.abstract: Stochastic computing (SC) encodes values as the probability of ones in random bit-streams, which allows arithmetic circuits with very low area and power and a natural tolerance to faults. The accuracy and security of an SC system depend on the quality of those bit-streams. Conventional generators build them from pseudo-random or quasi-random sequences, which are predictable, periodic, and correlated across streams drawn from the same generator. This work proposes three methods for converting the unbiased outputs of a true random number generator (TRNG) into stochastic bit-streams (SBS) with arbitrary target probabilities: a block extraction and comparison circuit, a counter-logic circuit, and a cascaded majority-logic pipeline. items.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
items.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations. However, realizing a scalable architecture that supports quantum error correction, qubit transport, wiring, and logical gate operations remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scalable dense silicon spin qubit architecture designed to support large-scale FTQC. The architecture consists of qubit memories, data qubit lanes, and cross junctions. Qubit memories store logical qubits encoded using the rotated surface code and support logical single-qubit operations. items.title: Low-barrier-height Hf$_\text{1-x}$Zr$_\text{x}$O$_2$ ferroelectric tunnel junctions with large ON-state currents
items.abstract: Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) hold great promise for nonvolatile memory, neuromorphic computing, and other applications. Hf$_\text{1-x}$Zr$_\text{x}$O$_2$ (HZO) has become a leading candidate for the tunnel barrier due primarily to its compatibility with CMOS technology. Recent advances on HZO based FTJs have highlighted the importance of understanding the electrical transport through a ferroelectric tunnel barrier for fulfilling the technological promises of FTJs. In this paper we report investigation of HZO FTJs featuring a barrier of ultrathin HZO ($\leq$5nm) measured down to a temperature of 2 K. Direct quantum tunneling was found to dominate at low temperatures, along with contributions from trap-assisted tunneling. As the temperature increases, conduction by thermal activation takes over. We developed a minimal model that accounts for all experimental observations, revealin...

items.title: Physics-Based TCAD Modeling of Nanowire Cryotrons with Coupled Superconducting and Thermal Dynamics
items.abstract: Nanowire cryotrons (nTrons) provide gate-controlled superconducting switching, current gain, and high-impedance outputs for cryogenic computing, detector readout, and superconductor-semiconductor interfaces. We develop a physics-based Sentaurus TCAD framework that couples time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau dynamics, separate electron and phonon energy equations, and mixed-mode circuit simulation. Superconducting terminal-current corrections connect the custom solver to the native electrical solution, linking local suppression of superconductivity, heating and cooling, and current redistribution in the external circuit. To our knowledge, this is the first Sentaurus-based mixed-mode TCAD implementation for nTrons. We calibrate the model against experimental switching data at six gate currents using a single parameter set. The model achieves an RMS load-current error below 1 $μ$A outside the sw...

items.title: Unveiling ferroelectricity in wafer-scale beta-phase In$_2$Se$_3$
items.abstract: Pushing ferroelectricity to the ultimate thickness limit is a central challenge for memory hardware, because conventional three-dimensional ferroelectrics degrade through depolarization and interfacial effects when thinned. Here we identify $β$-In$_2$Se$_3$, a van der Waals semiconductor regarded as centrosymmetric, as a host of bistable polar order arising from a picometre-scale distortion within each quintuple layer. The polar state has out-of-plane and in-plane components, is switched by a vertical electric field, and persists to the bilayer limit (~1.9 nm) with an estimated coercive field of 0.9 MV/cm and an apparent remanent polarization of 11.0 $μ$C/cm$^2$. Films grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on 2-inch wafers yield capacitor arrays with a switching-voltage spread below 5% across 100 devices, an endurance of $10^7$ cycles and a projected ten-year retention. items.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
items.abstract: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly. Agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) code against an executable integer reference that specifies the outputs and the stored state at every decoding step. They debug against public tests under fixed budgets; their frozen designs are graded on held-out token sequences, resets, memory stalls, and synthesis, and a second track asks them to speed up a correct design at nearly fixed area. items.title: A library-based approach for inverse reconstruction of cavity depth using angle-resolved cathodoluminescence
items.abstract: In nanofabrication processes, accurate metrology is a crucial step for obtaining control over the required critical dimensions in a device. Traditionally, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is used to obtain high resolution measurements of the lateral dimension, but obtaining depth information on a thick sample is more complex. In this work, we use angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (AR-CL) spectroscopy to resolve this third dimension. Using 30 keV electrons in the SEM, CL is created at the bottom of a micrometer scale cavity milled in a gold surface. We show that reflections of the CL off the cavity sidewalls produce an interferogram which is a sensitive probe for the cavity geometry. items.title: Electron spin relaxation and coherence times of silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
items.abstract: Color defect centers carrying electron spins in solid crystals like diamond and silicon carbide (SiC) are promising candidates for qubits and quantum sensors, with SiC material being particularly interesting due to its compatibility with the existing semiconductor technology. Here we investigated the electron spin properties of silicon vacancy centers (V1 and V2) both electron spin $S = 3/2$ in 4H-SiC in the temperature range $T=80-300$~K using electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR). The EPR spectrum shows central and satellite lines, where the former ones originate from V1 and V2 centers, as well as from unknown defect center X. items.title: Design, Testing and Calibration of the GAPS Experiment Si(Li) Tracker Readout ASIC: From the First Flight Campaign Toward the Second Mission Upgrade
items.abstract: The General Antiparticle Spectrometer (GAPS) is a balloon-borne experiment designed to perform three long-duration flights from Antarctica to search for low-energy cosmic antinuclei, in particular antideuterons, as an indirect signature of dark matter. Its detection method relies on the formation and decay of exotic atoms, identified through the emission of characteristic x-rays and the subsequent annihilation into secondary particles. At the core of the instrument is the silicon tracker, composed of lithium-drifted silicon detectors operated at -40°C and read out by a custom application-specific integrated circuit, SLIDER32, implemented in 180 nm CMOS technology. This thesis reports on the integration, calibration, and validation of the SLIDER32-based tracker readout electronics. Laboratory characterization of a tracker module with an Am-241 source and cosmic muons was complemented by c...

items.title: Certified minimax normal-scale mixtures for the logistic-normal integral
items.abstract: The logistic distribution function is a scale mixture of normal distribution functions, and Monahan and Stefanski approximate it by the $K$-term mixture $Λ(x) \approx \sum_{i} w_i Φ(s_i x)$ chosen to minimise the uniform error on the real line. Each such mixture reduces the logistic-normal integral to a sum of $K$ normal distribution functions with the mixture's uniform error bound. This integral is the expectation of a logistic sigmoid over a normal distribution in statistics and the Gauss-Fermi integral in semiconductor physics. Monahan and Stefanski tabulate constants for $K \le 8$ and conjecture that the optimal error equioscillates at $2K$ points, while above $K = 8$ the Remez exchange and local solvers stall at nonequioscillating stationary points. We prove that the tangent space of the mixture family is a Chebyshev system, which forces $2K$-point equioscillation at every interior...

items.title: First-principles phase diagram of monolayer CrS$_2$ polymorphs under biaxial strain and its sensitivity to the Hubbard U parameter
items.abstract: In correlated two-dimensional magnets the balance between competing electronic and magnetic phases is often set by the strength of the on-site Coulomb interaction, so that the predicted ground state can hinge on a parameter that is not uniquely defined. Monolayer CrS$_2$ lies squarely in this regime, hosting several energetically close polymorphs whose character ranges from non-magnetic semiconducting to magnetically ordered metallic. We therefore investigate, using DFT$+U$ within the generalized gradient approximation, the structural, magnetic, and electronic properties of the 1H, 1T, 1T$'$, and 1T$''$ polymorphs of monolayer CrS$_2$ under varying Hubbard interactions ($U=0$--$8$~eV) and biaxial strain ($-10\%$ to $+10\%$). items.title: N-Polar AlGaN/GaN Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor
items.abstract: Heterojunction bipolar transistors based on the III-Nitride systems have significantly lower performance than field effect transistors due to challenges associated with p-type doping of the base. N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBTs can overcome these challenges by polarization-induced holes in the base and base-emitter interface. We experimentally demonstrate the first N-polar AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on GaN substrate without emitter regrowth. The HBTs exhibit a peak current gain of approximately 15, peak differential current gain of approximately 18, and emitter-area-normalized peak current densities exceeding 20 kA/cm^2 and 66 kA/cm^2 for emitter areas of 10 x 10 um^2 and 3 x 10 um^2, respectively. The specific contact resistance for base is estimated 1.32 x 10^{-2} Ohm.cm^2. The open-base breakdown voltage is characterized...

items.title: Real-Time AI Acceleration on a 2D Spatial Dataflow Architecture
items.abstract: Machine Learning (ML) is increasingly being integrated into real-time systems, which makes the timing analysis of ML accelerators necessary. However, the most popular commercial accelerator, the Graphics Processing Unit (GPU), remains difficult to analyze as several aspects of its behavior, including scheduling of threads involved in single-instruction multiple-thread computations and memory access latency, are not fully documented. Spatial dataflow accelerators present an interesting alternative to GPUs, as they inherently support compute and memory partitioning. Data movement and computation locality are explicitly controlled by the programmer. In this work, we consider the Tenstorrent Blackhole, which is based on a commodity RISC-V architecture. It consists of a 2D grid of cores connected by Networks-on-Chip (NoCs), supporting a fully open software runtime. We profile the Blackhole pl...

items.title: Neural-operator acceleration of bidirectional phonon Boltzmann-Fourier coupling for multiscale heat transport in silicon fin arrays
items.abstract: Localized heating in semiconductor devices can produce non-diffusive phonon transport near heat-generating regions, while heat spreading through the surrounding substrate remains well described by Fourier conduction. We present a hybrid framework that couples a pretrained neural operator for the phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) within individual fins to a Fourier model of a shared substrate. To reduce the cost of repeated BTE solves across fin positions and coupling iterations, a DeepONet maps each fin's substrate-interface temperature and heating state to its temperature and heat-flux fields. The operator is trained on interface temperatures generated by a linearized proxy of the coupled problem, which avoids explicit training data collection from full coupled runs. items.title: Resilience of Entangling Gates to Spatiotemporally Correlated Noise
items.abstract: As quantum processors scale, spatially and temporally correlated noise is emerging as a limiting factor in the fidelity of multiqubit gates. Here we show that this makes the choice of entangling operation a first-order design decision: for two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, the CZ and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates exhibit a pronounced resilience to correlated noise relative to the SWAP gate, even though correlated fluctuations of the entangling interaction can degrade gate performance to a level comparable to that of local noise. We trace this hierarchy to the redistribution of noise-sensitive channels away from zero frequency and show it to hold for noise spectra dominated by low-frequency weight, including $1/f$ and Lorentzian. items.title: Generalized dielectric-dependent hybrid functional combining Gaussian and Yukawa screening
items.abstract: We develop a generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) for dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals that combines Gaussian and Yukawa-type screening functions to provide an accurate representation of the random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function. Through systematic fitting to RPA dielectric functions of semiconductors and insulators, and to the Lindhard dielectric function of the homogeneous electron gas, we demonstrate that GCAM significantly reduces errors in the model dielectric function across the full momentum range. However, despite this improved physical description of screening, band gap calculations reveal that GCAM yields larger errors compared to experiment than previous CAM approaches for wide-gap materials, but smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials. items.title: Scanning nanowire quantum dot with radio-frequency read-out
items.abstract: Scanning single-electron transistors (SETs) are highly sensitive local probes of charge and electric potential, but their integration with robust height control for scanning probe microscopy remains challenging. Furthermore, readout bandwidths are limited to tens of kHz, while characterizing faster charge dynamics is often of interest. Here, we present a scanning SET in the form of a nanowire (NW) quantum dot (QD) integrated at the apex of a non-contact atomic force microscopy (NC-AFM) cantilever. We demonstrate NC-AFM topographic imaging and local electrometry capability by mapping the electrostatic potential generated by a set of nanoscale voltage-biased gate electrodes. Comparison with electrostatic simulations shows agreement with the measured potential profiles. items.title: Centimetre-sized meteoroids from the active asteroid (3200) Phaethon: lunar impact flashes during the 2018 and 2025 Geminids
items.abstract: Centimetre-sized meteoroids released by the active asteroid (3200) Phaethon, parent of the Geminid meteor shower, probe the ejection of refractory material from a comet-asteroid transition object and the age of the stream; lunar impact flashes (LIFs) are the only ground-based technique that samples this size range. We determine the impact flux, mass and size distributions, and expected crater sizes of Geminid meteoroids on the Moon from campaigns at the 2018 and 2025 maxima, and test the stability of the centimetre-sized population over seven years. Both campaigns used the Nihon University 0.40 m "GUNDAM" telescope with CMOS video cameras at 60 fps, with candidates validated at independent stations; a common aperture-photometry pipeline calibrated in the Cousins R band gave peak magnitudes to 0.1-0.25 mag. items.title: Anatomy of orbital and spin responses in GaAs and Si: Hall, inverse Faraday, and magneto-optical Kerr effects
items.abstract: Magneto-optical signals in nonmagnetic semiconductors entangle spin and orbital contributions, both in angular-momentum generation and magneto-optical detection. We calculate these contributions for electron-doped GaAs and Si using density-functional theory, linear-response theory, and a second-order density-matrix treatment of the inverse Faraday effect. At small electron doping, the intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity exceeds its spin counterpart in magnitude, while the orbital contribution to light-induced magnetization dominates over broad photon-energy ranges. We show that orbital- and spin-resolved optical Hall and polar Kerr coefficients exhibit stronger sensitivity to orbital moments than to equal spin moments. items.title: Numerical simulations of CCP-2D GEC with sGMRES
items.abstract: Fluid models provide an efficient means of simulating the low-temperature gas discharges, which are important in semiconductor manufacturing. This work presents, to the best of our knowledge, the first systematic numerical framework for the Gaseous Electronics Conference (GEC) reference cell of the 2D capacitively coupled plasma (CCP). The framework employs a structured, nonuniform cylindrical mesh to resolve the spatial gradients. A semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is used for the Poisson's equation, while the implicit SG schemes are applied to the continuity equations and the electron energy equation. Both the explicit and and the implicit formulations based on the conventional drift-diffusion terms are also investigated. To solve the resulting large-scale linear systems, we introduce an incomplete LU (ILU)-preconditioned sketched GMRES (sGMRES) method as the solver. As far...

This review focuses on recent advances in THz modulation based on different materials including 2D semiconductors and metamaterials with attention to their response under external stimuli. items.abstract: Controlling polar domains in conducting materials by external fields could unlock polarization-based electronic functionalities, yet remains experimentally challenging. While mechanical actuation driven by local strain, stress, or strain gradients has been proposed as an external-voltage-free route, its experimental demonstration in relatively conducting polar materials remains limited. Here we demonstrate mechanically induced polar-domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave (CDW) semiconductor EuTe4 at room temperature, whose resistivity is on the order of 10 m$Ω$cm. Polarized-light microscopy and second-harmonic-generation measurements reveal CDW-induced in-plane polarization domains with an approximately 90 $^\circ$ domain configuration. items.title: Proposal for a cat-cluster-state machine gun
items.abstract: Non-Gaussian bosonic states such as the Schrödinger cat states are essential for continuous-variable quantum-information processing. A convenient and deterministic process for generating cat states is through the use of a Rabi interaction between a single bosonic mode and a spin which facilitates a state-dependent displacement. The lack of a Rabi interaction for propagating optical photons has rendered optical cat states elusive. Here, we show that the complex nonlinear scattering dynamics of a single-mode squeezed-vacuum state interacting with a quantum emitter can be engineered to produce a Rabi interaction between a quantum emitter and a propagating photon mode while the contributions from other orthogonal modes destructively interfere. items.title: Population of spin orbit-split-electron branches in semimetallic HgTe quantum wells
items.abstract: We present the results of experimental studies on magnetoresistance, the Hall effect, and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations performed in gated heterostructures with HgTe-based gapless semiconductor quantum wells. We show that in quantum wells with widths corresponding to a semimetallic charge carrier spectrum, electrons, in contrast to the idealized model, populate both spin-orbit-split branches of the spectrum. This occurs regardless of whether the Fermi level lies exclusively in the conduction band or within the conduction-valence band overlap region.

items.abstract: Multi-agent frameworks are attracting increasing attention as a means of autonomously driving complex, long-running workflows in first-principles materials modeling. items.title: JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer
items.abstract: As semiconductor device dimensions approach phonon mean free paths, heat transport enters ballistic and quasi-ballistic regimes where Fourier's law becomes inadequate. The phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) describes these nonequilibrium effects but presents significant computational challenges. This work introduces JAX-Nano, a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable phonon BTE solver for nanoscale heat transport. The solver integrates steady-state and transient BTE formulations within a unified finite-volume framework, supporting structured and unstructured meshes, mode-resolved transport, phonon scattering, volumetric heat generation, and multiple boundary conditions. Automatic differentiation enables gradient computation with respect to transport properties, boundary conditions, heat-generation rates, and geometric parameters without separately derived adjoint equations. items.title: First-Principles Investigation of the {ScSe2} TMDs Monolayer: Structural Stability, Electronic and Optical Properties
items.abstract: We present an ab initio investigation of the {ScSe2} monolayer using density functional theory (DFT), as employed in the CP2K code, to assess its structural stability and electronic properties. The electronic behavior of both phases is governed by the local coordination environment of scandium and the associated lifting of degeneracy of its $3d$ orbitals. The valence bands (VBs) are dominated by {Se}$-4p$ states in both phases, while the states near the Fermi level distinguish the metallic 1T phase from the semiconducting 2H phase. Optical response calculations reveal markedly different spectral signatures for the two polymorphs. Two findings emerge from this study: a polymorphism-driven metal-to-semiconductor transition without any change in chemical composition and distinct optical responses relevant to phase-selective optoelectronic devices.

items.title: CHARMS250V1: A Cryogenic Front-End ASIC for Low-Noise Readout of Charge or Light Signals in Noble Liquid Detectors
items.abstract: This work presents the design and measurement results of CHARMS250V1, a next-generation cryogenic front-end application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed using a 65 nm CMOS process. It is designed for low-noise readout of charge or light signals generated in noble liquid detectors. CHARMS250V1 is a single channel prototype whose design in the future will be integrated within a 16-channel ASIC. It comprises pre-amplification and pulse shaping stages that provide programmable charge gain between 4.3 mV/fC and 25 mV/fC, peaking time programmable between 250 ns and 2 us, and programmable baseline of either 200 mV or 900 mV for processing of unipolar and bipolar signals, respectively.

This study explores the relationship between stoichiometry, structural phase, and electronic transport in niobium sulfoselenide (NbSxSe2-x) thin films. In this study, low-dimensional TMD films were grown with molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) to investigate the effects of varying chalcogen (sulfur and selenium) content in NbSxSe2-x alloys. We focus on tuning electrical resistivity along with the transition from metallic-to-semiconducting behavior through compositional control. These MBE grown films were characterized using in-vacuo x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) to analyze the chemical composition. items.title: Optical Scintillation Imaging for Dynamic Source Tracking Dosimetry During Prostate HDR Brachytherapy
items.abstract: High-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy is highly conformal, but its accuracy depends on catheter and source placement, and clinical workflows lack real-time in vivo dosimetry (IVD) that verifies delivery without disrupting the procedure. We characterize a scintillator-based optical dosimeter integrated into a transrectal probe that tracks source position, speed, dose rate, and time-resolved cumulative dose. A 67 mm x 5 mm line scintillator is imaged by a CMOS camera through a 30-degree endoscopic lens; geometric and flat-field corrections remove barrel distortion and vignetting. Absolute dose was calibrated with a TOPAS Monte Carlo model of the probe's air-cavity geometry. The system was validated in a water phantom with an Ir-192 source and needles at radial offsets of 7, 10, and 15 mm. items.title: Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots
items.abstract: Tuning electrostatically defined quantum dots remains a primary bottleneck in the scalability of semiconductor spin qubits. While existing solutions rely on machine learning algorithms, these approaches require global information, introduce latency bottlenecks, and tax the limited cooling power available at cryogenic stages. Here, we demonstrate an FPGA-in-the-loop learning paradigm that bypasses digital computing overhead by utilizing multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) for tuning. Implemented on an FPGA and an emulated quantum dot device, our system autonomously tracks environmental drift, dynamically recovers from discrete charge jumps, and maintains steady-state stabilization in low signal-to-noise ratio regimes, without prior knowledge of the device's cross-capacitance matrix. items.title: Coherence Lengths of Laser Pointers
items.abstract: We report on the coherence lengths of low-cost green laser pointers in the midst of multimodal behavior using an optical interferometer based on noncollinear beam geometries and a CMOS detector array. Examined devices include three diode lasers and a frequency-doubled neodymium-emission diode-pumped solid state (DPSS) laser. Coherence length measurements are variable among devices, but values can nevertheless regularly exceed 10 cm. The work serves as a template for an advanced undergraduate physics laboratory experiment and may inspire new kinds of laser pointer devices utilizing interference effects as operative principles.

items.abstract: Closing the final 5%-15% of code and functional coverage remains a major schedule bottleneck in silicon tapeouts. Existing LLM-based coverage closure loops feed raw uncovered RTL lines or branches directly into iterative prompts, failing on industrial subsystems due to: (1) token and context explosion from querying thousands of correlated holes independently; (2) illegal stimulus that violates cross-signal invariants and yields dirty coverage; and (3) unsafe exclusion hallucination on structurally unreachable dead code. items.abstract: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. items.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
items.abstract: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. items.title: Topology-Enabled Self-Verification of Quantum Hall Resistance Standards
items.abstract: The scaling of multi-element quantized Hall array resistance standards necessitates rigorous validation that internal quantization has not broken down without relying on the verification of dissipationless edge state transport. One proposed solution is to use a Symmetric Precision Quantization Reliability criterion, a mathematical framework that statistically assures such validation strictly through outer terminal measurements of Cn-symmetric designs. This criterion essentially bounds the likelihood of hidden localized defects arising from quantum Hall breakdown and has potential uses in quantum computing and semiconductor testing but is presented in the context of its application toward quantum electrical standards.

items.abstract: In this work, we investigate thermal transport in a set of thin-film layers used in modern HEMT designs. For modeling the specific samples at hand, the latter are fitted to thermal conductivity data measured with Time-Domain Thermoreflectance (TDTR). items.title: CRAFT: Analog Circuit Design by Reasoning LLM Agents from Pre-Computed Lookup Tables
items.abstract: Automated analog circuit sizing methods, from black-box optimizers to recent large language model (LLM) agents, typically search the design space with a SPICE simulator in the loop, whereas an experienced designer works out a design by hand analysis. This paper presents CRAFT, a flow in which an LLM agent designs a given topology by calculation, as a designer does, and without an initial sizing. The agent works only through DeX, a service that uses pre-computed lookup tables to provide device characteristics and to solve the whole netlist for its operating point and small-signal response. It thus designs without SPICE, and every final design is verified independently in HSPICE. We test CRAFT on four circuits in a commercial 28 nm process; the largest is a 37-transistor three-stage amplifier with 53 design variables, 20 specifications and 74 saturation constraints. items.title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
items.abstract: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors. items.title: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
items.abstract: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu$_2$O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the scalability and advanced fabrication of integrated photonics. Here we demonstrate a monolithic, CMOS-compatible interface of Cu$_2$O Rydberg excitons with a SiN$_x$ nanophotonic waveguide. items.abstract: This work analyzes the high-frequency performance constraints of AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) and proposes a novel band-engineered graded base N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBT and evaluates the RF performances. Unlike conventional p-GaN base designs, we propose a graded base in the N-polar orientation which offers polarization-induced hole accumulation with quasi-electric field-assisted minority carrier transport. The proposed design simultaneously mitigates the longstanding current crowding, Webster effect, and conventional base resistance limitations. Using well-calibrated two-dimensional TCAD simulations, the proposed compositionally graded base HBT projects peak f_T/f_{MAX} of 190/200 GHz with a power density (V_{BR}I_{MAX}/8 > 20 W/mm), offering a promising pathway toward simultaneous high-frequency and high-power GaN millimeter-wave electronics.

items.title: Optical readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors with SiPMs
items.abstract: Scintillation light readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors (MPGDs) is used for imaging and track reconstruction applications including in optical Time Projection Chambers (TPC). Typically, high resolution CCD or CMOS imaging sensors are used and PMTs can be employed to obtain auxiliary timing information. We report on the optical readout of MPGDs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) which enables limited spatial resolution. Arrays of SiPMs were used to read out Gaseous Electron Multipliers (GEMs) and Glass Micromegas amplification stages. Center of gravity reconstruction of hit positions yields a spatial resolution of approximately 1.35 mm for signals shared across multiple SiPMs. High gain of the amplification stage as well as the SiPMs enables good signal sharing and is advantageous for position reconstruction.

items.title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
items.abstract: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis. Consequently, sub-digital processors could potentially offer a viable, near-term solution to drastically reduce the energy demands of AI.

items.title: Ultrafast Successive Control and Electrical Detection of Long-Lived Valley Polarization in Room-Temperature Germanium
items.abstract: Germanium (Ge) hosts four degenerate valleys in the conduction band minima, and their highly anisotropic effective masses offer a valley degree of freedom in transport phenomena via anisotropic conductivity. Using time- and polarization-resolved terahertz spectroscopy combined with deformation potential theory, we reveal a valley relaxation time reaching 10 ps near the band edge of Ge(001) at room temperature, long enough to detect the valley polarization in electrical transport measurements. We also demonstrate sub-picosecond complete reversal of valley polarization by off-resonant light pulses at extremely low energy consumption. These results pave the way for room-temperature valleytronics based on bulk indirect-gap semiconductors compatible with existing electronics.

items.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
items.abstract: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions. Today's solid-state quantum processors are different -- every qubit receives instructions from outside the chip via its own dedicated control line, and error correction adds a further torrent of syndrome data that is transported off-chip. Here we show that the external control of a quantum chip can be greatly simplified. We propose a fault-tolerant architecture for universal quantum computation, inspired by modern classical processors, in which quantum information flows through a fixed, clocked device, propelled by local gates in a planar array. items.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field inse...

items.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
items.abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. The strongest general-purpose model scores only 53.7%, and on matched...

items.title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
items.abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. items.title: BROAD: Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM
items.abstract: Processing-using-memory (PUM) architectures perform computation directly within DRAM to reduce costly data movement between memory and processors. Because charge-sharing operations are confined to individual bitlines, existing DRAM-PUM architectures reorganize data into column-oriented, bit-serial representations. This organization is fundamentally incompatible with the row-oriented, word-parallel layouts used by conventional processors and accelerators, requiring expensive data-layout transformations whenever computation transitions between PUM and conventional execution. In this paper, we present BROAD, or Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM. BROAD augments the DRAM subarray with two lightweight extensions: migration cells that enable localized horizontal data movement between neighboring bitlines and inversion cells that provide efficient in-array logical inversion. items.title: SPLASH: Co-Designing Flash-Aware Sparse Attention with a Virtualized HBM-HBF Hierarchy
items.abstract: As context lengths, request lifetimes and concurrency grow, the key-value (KV) cache dominates memory usage in large language model (LLM) inference. High-bandwidth memory (HBM), the memory on contemporary GPUs, achieves far higher bandwidth than off-package memory, yet its capacity, bounded by DRAM density, has not kept pace with this demand. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF), an emerging memory technology, bridges this gap, combining the advanced packaging of HBM with the density of flash to deliver terabyte-scale capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth. Exploiting this capacity for long-context KV caches, however, requires hiding the vastly different physical characteristics of flash from the GPU while keeping decode interactive. We therefore introduce Splash, an architecture that virtualizes HBM and HBF for the KV cache. We architect custom HBM and HBF base dies with novel memory and flash cont...

items.title: Probing proximity-induced superconductivity in bilayer graphene using gate-defined quantum dots
items.abstract: Van der Waals heterostructures enable the combination of two-dimensional (2D) materials with different electronic properties in a single device. Bilayer graphene (BLG) is particularly attractive as its electrically tunable band gap enables local control of tunnel barriers and quantum dots (QDs). Here, we realize an all-2D hybrid platform based on BLG proximitized by superconducting NbSe$_2$. Using electrostatic gates, we define tunnel barriers and QDs at different distances from the superconductor-semiconductor interface. The QDs serve as local spectroscopic probes of the proximitized BLG channel, forming tunable superconductor-quantum dot-normal conductor junctions. Coulomb blockade and finite-bias spectroscopy reveal a proximity-induced superconducting gap of up to $80\,\mathrm{μeV}$ and allow to track its evolution with distance from the NbSe$_2$ contact. items.title: Continuous-Wave Operation at 30 MV/m of a Superconducting Radio-Frequency Gun Cryomodule with an Exchangeable Cathode Plug
items.abstract: A prototype 185.7 MHz superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) electron gun cryomodule has been developed for the proposed LCLS-II-HE Low Emittance Injector at SLAC. It has an in-situ ultra-high-vacuum exchangeable cathode plug system compatible with semiconductor photocathodes. With a copper plug, the gun achieved continuous-wave RF operation at a cathode field of 30 MV/m. No measurable degradation was observed after plug removal and reinsertion with the cavity at 4.4 K. This result is a significant improvement over past continuous-wave SRF gun systems with exchangeable plugs.

items.title: Heteroepitaxial Growth of PbSe on InP via III-V Buffer Layers
items.abstract: Detector cost remains a barrier to the widespread adoption of mid-wave infrared (3-5 micron) technology. PbSe, an inexpensive narrow band gap IV-VI semiconductor that has been used since the early 1940s, delivers high performance for infrared detection despite the abundance of grain boundaries in polycrystalline films. Epitaxial growth, however, could provide superior crystalline quality and interfaces, but suitable substrates remain limited for PbSe. Recent PbSe heteroepitaxy has focused primarily on III-V, II-VI and group-IV substrates that each offer a comparatively narrow range of lattice-matched alloys for heterostructure engineering. Here we show that InP-based heteroepitaxy provides access to a broader materials platform while limiting the lattice mismatch with PbSe to approximately 4%. items.title: Josephson effect in bipolar magnetic semiconductors
items.abstract: We theoretically investigate equilibrium currents in a one-dimensional Josephson junction incorporating a bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS). We show that the intrinsic exchange splitting of the spin-resolved bands enables purely electrical control of the $0$--$π$ transition through gate-tunable modulation of the BMS chemical potential, eliminating the need for an external magnetic field. This provides a viable route toward electrically tunable $π$-junction behavior and highlights the potential of BMS-based Josephson devices for phase-controllable superconducting electronics. Furthermore, in the presence of Rashba spin--orbit coupling, we find an anomalous Josephson effect characterized by a finite equilibrium supercurrent at zero phase difference. items.title: OpenTherm: A Unified and Progressive Benchmark for 2.5D/3D-IC Thermal Prediction
items.abstract: Accurate and efficient chip thermal prediction is essential for advanced packaging design. In recent years, deep learning-based thermal predictors have made significant progress, achieving high prediction accuracy while substantially reducing computational costs. However, differences in datasets, simulators, and evaluation protocols hinder direct comparison of existing methods and systematic assessment of their generalization across design variations and cross-package transfer scenarios. We introduce OpenTherm, an open benchmark combining 32,000 established 3D-IC samples with 50,000 new 2.5D chiplet samples generated with the open-source HotSpot simulator. It provides fixed data splits, a common input representation, and shared evaluation tools. items.title: Dual-Mode Exciton Coupling in Epitaxially Registered Organic-Inorganic 2D Heterocrystals
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) heterocrystals comprising molecules and semiconductors can serve as an ideal platform for studying interfacial excitons and for future optoelectronic applications, yet the energy and charge flow across these atomically sharp interfaces remain unclear. In this work, we investigated PTCDA-MoS2 as a prototypical 2D organic-inorganic heterostructure and revealed dual-mode exciton coupling between the constituent crystals. Monolayer-resolved PTCDA molecular crystals were grown on monolayer MoS2 via physical vapor assembly, and their crystallographic details, including the stacking angle, were determined by electron diffraction. Upon the formation of the heterostructures, PTCDA's photoluminescence was completely quenched because of organic-to-inorganic hole transfer, whereas that of MoS2 increased markedly with PTCDA thickness. items.title: First-principles carrier mobility and optical absorption of strained ZnO with self-consistent Hubbard interactions
items.abstract: Carrier mobility and optical absorption are key performance parameters of oxide semiconductors in transparent and flexible displays. We use a newly developed density-functional perturbation theory with a self-consistent Hubbard correction (DFPT+U) to study phonon-limited electron transport and phonon-assisted optical absorption in strained zinc oxide (ZnO). This parameter-free approach accounts for electron-phonon interactions and on-site correlation effects simultaneously. Electronic structures and phonon dispersions are computed under three distinct uniaxial strain directions. Uniaxial tensile strain up to 4.8% along [\bar110] is found to increase the room-temperature electron mobility by 19% while leaving visible-range optical absorption essentially unchanged. These results demonstrate that moderate strain can selectively enhance carrier transport without degrading optical transparenc...

items.title: Direct visualization of charge dynamics by Pockels imaging in optoelectronics
items.abstract: Understanding charge dynamics in optoelectronic devices is essential because it governs carrier transport, signal evolution, and device performance. Yet, experimental access to the spatiotemporal evolution of charge remains limited. Here, we introduce Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI), a sensitive, quantitative, and non-invasive pump-probe technique based on the linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect. CDPI images the electric-field wave associated with traveling photogenerated carriers and reveals the evolution of charge clouds in space and time. This provides direct access to fundamental transport processes, including drift, diffusion, carrier-carrier interactions, trapping, and detrapping. items.title: 2D Transport in an in-plane magnetic field
items.abstract: A parallel in-plane magnetic field could, in principle, distinguish between two competing physical scenarios for the experimentally observed density-tuned 2D metal-insulator transition (where decreasing the carrier density leads to a crossover from an effective metal to an effective insulator): Wigner crystallization or Anderson localization. Since the main scattering mechanism in 2D doped semiconductors arises from screened random charged impurities and screening in turn depends on the electronic density of states, the in-plane magnetic field could distinguish between the two by decreasing screening through spin polarization and this enhances the effective critical density for Anderson localization compared with Wigner crystallization.
